This document provides a comprehensive technical overview of the **Fast Path Triangulation Pipeline**, **Intermediate Quadratic Decomposition**, and **Dynamic Viewport-Adaptive Pixel-Space Level of Detail (LOD)** in Retiam.
Retiam provides dual rendering strategies for 2D/3D vector paths and composite SVGs:

cells.text: Analytical Signed Distance Fields (SDF) + multi-pass stencil chains
CPU Triangulation (Earcut / Polygon-Clipping) + GPU Stroke Compute
Standard triangle rasterization with uber-shader instance switching
Infinite zoom precision, custom procedural fragment shaders, complex boolean clipping
High-density SVGs (e.g. 50,000+ subpaths), real-time procedural animations, high-framerate rendering
Naturally continuous via GPU fragment raymarching
Dynamic in-place re-tessellation via Hysteresis-governed screen-space error

blocks.text: 2. Decomposition Architecture: Intermediate Quadratic vs. Direct Line

When rendering vector paths in `fast` mode, curves must be flattened into linear polylines (`Vec2[][]`) before triangulation. Retiam employs an **Intermediate Quadratic Contour Representation** (`rawContours: number[][]`).

flowchart LR
    A["SVG Path String ('d')"] -->|"One-Time Decode (C -> Q, A -> Q)"| B["Flat Numeric Buffers (rawContours: number[][])"]
    B -->|"flattenContours(rawContours, tolerance)"| C["Linear Polylines (Vec2[][])"]
    C --> D["Fill Triangulation (Earcut / Martinez-Rueda)"]
    C --> E["GPU Stroke Extrusion Compute"]
    
    subgraph "Continuous Viewport LOD Loop"
        F["Camera Zoom / Movement"] -->|"Check Hysteresis Window"| G{"Current Pixel Error Drifts Outside Bounds?"}
        G -->|"Yes (6.0x faster)"| B
        G -->|"No"| H["Retain Active Geometry (0 buffer rebuilds)"]
    end

blocks.text: Why Intermediate Quadratic is 6.0x Faster than Direct Decomposition
In benchmarks across complex scenes (`paris-30k.svg` containing 50,620 subpaths):

children: Direct decomposition must execute regex tokenization (`parsePath`), absolute normalization (`absolutize`), and arc matrix transformations on every frame or zoom event.
The intermediate representation parses the string **only once** into contiguous primitive `number[]` arrays (`[x0, y0, cx, cy, x1, y1, ...]`).

items.text: **Reduced Arithmetic Complexity of de Casteljau Recursion**:
children: Cubic Bézier curves ($C$) have 4 control points, requiring **6 intermediate point evaluations** per recursion step ($P_{01}, P_{12}, P_{23}, P_{012}, P_{123}, P_{0123}$) and deeper recursion trees.

Quadratic Bézier curves ($Q$) have 3 control points, requiring only **3 intermediate point evaluations** ($P_{01}, P_{12}, P_{012}$) and simple scalar midpoint distance checks ($\text{dist}^2 = \frac{1}{4}((P_1.x - \text{mid}.x)^2 + (P_1.y - \text{mid}.y)^2)$).
`rawContours` stores primitive numbers contiguously, preventing the allocation of millions of transient `Vec2` instances on the JavaScript heap.

blocks.text: 3. Screen-Space Pixel Tolerance & Dynamic Adaptive LOD
Geometric `tolerance` is defined in local model units. Retiam converts target screen-pixel tolerances into equivalent local tolerances based on camera optics and world transformations.

items: $T_{\text{pixel}}$ = Target allowable screen-space curve deviation in pixels (e.g. $1.0\text{ px}$)

blocks.text: Given camera field of view $\theta$ (in radians), camera world position $\mathbf{C}$, entity world position $\mathbf{E}$, and forward unit vector $\mathbf{F}$:

blocks.tex: \text{Pixels Per Local Unit} = \text{Pixels Per World Unit} \times S_{\text{world}}

blocks.text: To prevent constant re-tessellation ("jitter" / buffer thrashing) while smoothly animating or slightly adjusting the camera, Retiam evaluates a hysteresis window with a ratio-safe lower bound:

blocks.tex: \text{Lower Limit} = \begin{cases} T_{\text{target}} - \Delta T & \text{if } \Delta T < T_{\text{target}} \\ \frac{T_{\text{target}}}{1 + \frac{\Delta T}{T_{\text{target}}}} & \text{if } \Delta T \ge T_{\text{target}} \end{cases}

items: **Zoom In ($\text{error} > \text{Upper Limit}$)**: Automatically refines mesh resolution, adding subdivisions to maintain sub-pixel curve smoothness.
**Zoom Out ($\text{error} < \text{Lower Limit}$)**: Automatically simplifies mesh resolution, decreasing vertex counts to save GPU memory and vertex shader work.
**Inside Window ($\text{Lower Limit} \le \text{error} \le \text{Upper Limit}$)**: **Zero work** — existing vertex/index allocations remain untouched.

blocks.text: For complex compound shapes and typography glyphs (e.g. inner counters in letters 'R', 'e', 'd', 'B', 'a'):

children: Resolves overlapping and self-intersecting loops with even-odd or non-zero winding fill rules via `polygon-clipping`.

items.text: **Earcut Fallback with Interior Chord Test Points**:
children: When using direct ear clipping, hole detection identifies inner rings using polygon-in-polygon centroid and interior-chord test points.
Duplicate closing vertices on outer rings and hole boundaries are stripped prior to earcut indexing, preventing degenerate zero-area triangles.
